pull.title: validation: prefetch blocks while connecting
pull.body:
**Problem:** Block reading and decoding currently happen before block connection, even though loading is mostly I/O-bound and validation is CPU-bound.

This is a follow-up to [#35295](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35295), which parallelized input prevout fetching during block connection.

**Fix:** Route block loading through a block fetcher, add synchronous one-block read-ahead, then move the read to a lazy single-worker pool. Subsequent commits queue several reads and make the queue and worker count configurable.

**Credit:** The idea comes from [bitcoindev1337](https://bitcoin-irc.chaincode.com/bitcoin-core-dev/2026-08-11#1245429), who had already implemented a similar solution and reported comparable results.

<details><summary>Final benchmark results: 1.28x reindex-chainstate on SSD, 1.20x IBD on HDD</summary>

refactor: extract blocks passed to validation

`ActivateBestChain()` filters the caller-provided block by the selected most-work hash before calling `ActivateBestChainStep()`.
The step passes it to `ConnectTip()` only at the matching index, and extracting both selections into `block_to_connect` makes this relationship explicit.
The extraction leaves both conditions unchanged and keeps this mechanical preparation separate from the following `BlockFetcher` wiring.

refactor: route provided block through fetcher

`ActivateBestChain()` is the only caller of `ActivateBestChainStep()` and already filters the provided block to `index_most_work` before calling it.

Store that result in `BlockFetcher` while retaining the existing `pindexConnect == &index_most_work` check.
This preserves which block reaches `ConnectTip()` and leaves disk reads unchanged.

author Lőrinc <pap.lorinc@gmail.com> 1786936601 -0700
committer Lőrinc <pap.lorinc@gmail.com> 1787005185 -0700

validation: read one block ahead synchronously

`BlockFetcher` initially supplies only the caller-provided `index_most_work` block, leaving every other block for `ConnectTip()` to read synchronously.

Extend it to read and retain the next available block before connecting the current block.
Matching each result by hash preserves the provided-block restriction while allowing ancestors to use read-ahead.
A failed read returns no block, so `ConnectTip()` retries it synchronously.

`feature_reindex.py` covers cached-block consumption and verifies that synchronous read-ahead starts no worker.

committer Lőrinc <pap.lorinc@gmail.com> 1787005185 -0700

validation: read one block ahead on a worker

`BlockFetcher` reads the next block synchronously before connecting the current block, leaving both operations serialized.

Run the pending read on a lazily started single-worker `ThreadPool` so it overlaps the current block connection.
At the next connection attempt, consume the future and let `ConnectTip()` retry failed reads synchronously.

Extend reindex coverage to require worker startup while ordinary one-block generation starts no worker.

Co-authored-by: bitcoindev1337

author Lőrinc <pap.lorinc@gmail.com> 1787003692 -0700
committer Lőrinc <pap.lorinc@gmail.com> 1787005364 -0700

validation: queue several blocks for read-ahead

`BlockFetcher` initially keeps one pending read on one worker, limiting read-ahead to a single block at a time.

Replace the single future with a queue of 4 reads and start 4 workers, refilling only after the queue drains.
Upcoming blocks are often nearby in block files, so reading them together may benefit from the OS file cache.

Extend reindex coverage to require all four workers.

validation: configure block read-ahead

`BlockFetcher` initially uses four workers and queues four blocks at a time, with both counts fixed in code.

Expose this shared count through `-blockfetchpar` so one option controls both limits.
Use 0 to disable read-ahead, reject negative values, and clamp larger values to `MAX_BLOCKFETCH_THREADS`.

Extend argument and reindex coverage for disabled, default, and two-worker configurations.

comments.body:
This is creating a new ThreadPool on each invocation of `ActivateBestChain`. This is what's causing the logs in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36000#issuecomment-5326868873. The `BlockFetcher` or at least a shared pointer to a `ThreadPool` that can be passed to it should be owned by the `Chainstate`, so it can keep the fetcher threads alive throughout IBD.

This works fine for `-reindex-chainstate`, because it is one long `ActivateBestChain` call. But for IBD this gets called many times.
